overview: Snivvian (Humanoid mammal) is native to Cadomai and ranks among the most consequential species in galactic history. Snivvian artists from Cadomai produce work under harsh seasonal lockdowns; their proboscises and empathy-driven culture favor storytelling professions.
history:
The Snivvian (humanoid mammal) trace their deepest roots to Cadomai, where fossil beds, oral traditions, and surviving ruins suggest millennia of uninterrupted development. Snivvian evolutionary history on Cadomai intertwines with humanoid mammal adaptation, local predator cycles, and early hyperspace contact logs preserved in both Jedi and Sith archives. Galactic surveyors first catalogued Snivvian populations during the expansion of the Old Republic, though local records often predate offworld contact by thousands of years. Across films, Clone Wars, Rebels, Mandalorian, Ahsoka, KOTOR, KOTOR II, The Old Republic, and Sith Empire chronicles, Snivvian history is treated as foundational rather than peripheral.

In the Ancient Era and early Old Republic, Snivvian societies on Cadomai established trade routes, planetary defense, and Force traditions that later empires would inherit or suppress. Ancient Snivvian polities negotiated with Rakatan remnants, Sith emissaries, and Core Founders; archaeological teams still uncover Cadomai ruins that rewrite pre-Republic timelines. Archaeologists still debate how much of modern Snivvian identity was shaped by Rakatan influence, Infinite Empire collapse, and the long shadow of the Sith. High Republic archives mention Snivvian delegations, warriors, and artisans whose contributions were later rediscovered only through holocrons and battlefield inscriptions.

From the Clone Wars through the Imperial Era and into the New Republic, Snivvian diaspora communities appeared on every major trade lane and war front. Modern Snivvian diaspora appear in Clone Wars battlefronts, Rebels cells, Mandalorian guild halls, and Ahsoka-era investigations—often as the decisive local expert outsiders underestimated. Mandalorian-era intelligence briefings and Ahsoka-era reconstructions confirm that Snivvian networks remained active even when their homeworld fell under occupation or blockade. Sequel-era historians now treat Snivvian migration patterns as a map of galactic trauma and renewal, not mere demographic noise.

Snivvian fought in the galaxy's defining wars—not only as soldiers but as spies, healers, smugglers, and refugees whose choices shifted battle outcomes. Snivvian veterans fought in the Jedi Civil War (KOTOR), Sith Empire returns (TOR), Clone Wars sector campaigns, and the Galactic Civil War with tactics shaped by Cadomai's geography. KOTOR and KOTOR II document Snivvian involvement in the Jedi Civil War, while TOR and Sith Empire materials show parallel struggles against the Eternal Empire and Dread Masters. Rebels and Clone Wars episodes repeatedly demonstrate that a single Snivvian leader can rally a sector or, conversely, expose a conspiracy that topples a fleet.
significance:
Biologically, the Snivvian display traits typical of humanoid mammal life adapted to Cadomai's gravity, atmosphere, and seasonal extremes. Snivvian physiology—documented in Republic medical droids and Imperial biometrics—explains survival rates under occupation, labor extraction, and frontline service across eras. Medics note that Snivvian physiology interacts with cybernetics, clone templates, and Force healing in ways that are well documented in Republic medical journals. Geneticists argue that Snivvian resilience under occupation and exile explains much of their survival rate across the Rim and Unknown Regions.

Snivvian culture encodes memory through art, ritual, cuisine, and language dialects that survive even when homeworld cities are bombed flat. Snivvian rituals, language dialects, and art forms survived offworld commodification; cultural revival movements on Cadomai accelerated after the Empire's collapse. Both Jedi and Sith sources acknowledge Snivvian spiritual practices, though each tradition interprets those practices through its own doctrine of attachment and power. Living Snivvian communities on Coruscant, Nar Shaddaa, and Ferrix-style industrial worlds prove that culture is portable when homeworld sovereignty is not.

The galactic impact of the Snivvian exceeds what population tables suggest: their merchants, admirals, crime lords, and senators rewrote trade law and fleet doctrine. Galactic historians cite Snivvian merchants, soldiers, Force users, and criminals as pivot points in treaties, fleet battles, and underworld realignments from the Old Republic to the Sequel Era. Historians credit Snivvian innovators with breakthroughs in hyperspace navigation, droid ethics debates, and post-Imperial reconciliation councils. Whether aligned with the Republic, the Separatists, the Rebellion, or independent Mandalorian clans, Snivvian choices remain reference points in every major era study.
